title: Common domination of marked nodal models over a discrete valuation ring
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For $i=1,2$, let $X_i\to S$ be projective [def-kun-projective], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty connected reduced one-dimensional geometric fibres having only ordinary double points, and let $a_{i1},\ldots,a_{in}$ be pairwise disjoint sections in the relative smooth locus. These are marked nodal families in the terminology of [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction], with no positivity assumption. Let $u:(X_1)_K\xrightarrow{\sim}(X_2)_K$ be a $K$-isomorphism carrying $a_{1j,K}$ to $a_{2\sigma(j),K}$ for a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. There exist a projective flat finitely presented marked nodal family $Y\to S$ with disjoint smooth sections $b_1,\ldots,b_n$, proper $S$-morphisms $p_i:Y\to X_i$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], and finite sets $Z_i$ of closed points of the special fibres of $X_i$, such that $p_i^{-1}(X_i\setminus Z_i)\to X_i\setminus Z_i$ is an isomorphism, $(p_2)_K=u\circ(p_1)_K$, $p_1b_j=a_{1j}$, and $p_2b_j=a_{2\sigma(j)}$. In particular both $(p_i)_K$ are isomorphisms. No smoothness of the generic fibres, stability, completeness, excellence, or extension of $R$ is assumed. The case $n=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Agent marked and persistently nodal extension of the common-resolution construction of Tag 0C5S (lemma-birational-regular-surfaces), combined in the smooth-generic case with models.tex Tag 0CDE (lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal). Those tags do not themselves state this nodal-generic, semistable common-model result. A precise reference for the conductor-and-marking version is WANTED: Knudsen, The projectivity of the moduli space of stable curves II, sections 1--2.

proof.text: Normalize persistent nodes. The generic identification and integral-closure uniqueness identify $B\to N$ for both models; write $X_i=C_i\amalg_BN$. Markings lift away from $B$. Regularize $C_i$ to $T_i$, unchanged generically and near branches and markings. The component-comparison lemma matches integral regular surface components and supplies comparisons with special-fibre centres. Choose minimum length on each pair. The minimum ranges over sequences equipped with the second comparison map.

source.place: Agent assembly of persistent normalization (0CDD) and regularization (0CDE); component-comparison statement supplies matched surfaces and special-centred comparisons.

proof.text: Apply the good-centre criterion to each pair. Induct on its sequence: $T_i$ starts regular projective flat fp nodal with smooth generic fibre; each centre is smooth with finite separable residue field, so fibre defects preserves these properties and gives nonempty geometrically connected blowup fibres. Their finite disjoint union $W$ has these properties and maps to both $C_i$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the extracted minimum-length good-centre criterion and the point-blowup fibre-defect preservation statement (0AGQ).

proof.text: Projectivity gives properness. Extend $B_K\to W_K$ at every closed-point DVR of $B$ by proper valuative extension; spread to neighbourhoods and glue by separated dense-open equality. Flatness makes $B_K$ schematically dense. Extend each marking over $R$ similarly. Separated uniqueness fixes their composites to both $T_i$ and $C_i$, including the marking permutation. Etale-section avoidance makes the lifts smooth. Disjoint images in $C_1$ give disjoint lifts. Closed-immersion cancellation for $B\to W\to C_1$ makes the branch lift closed.

source.place: Agent extension of branches and markings by proper valuative extension, local-map spreading, separated gluing and the extracted regular-node avoidance statement (0CDD/0CDC).

proof.text: Pinch $B\hookrightarrow W$ along $B\to N$: the pinching theorem gives projective flat fp nodal $Y=W\amalg_BN$. Applied to $B\hookrightarrow C_i$ and $B\to N$ it gives a pushout which by uniqueness is $X_i$; so $C_i\to X_i$ is finite surjective, the square is cartesian, $N\to X_i$ is closed, and the square restricts to pushouts over opens and commutes with geometric-fibre base change. The universal property of $Y$ gives $p_i:Y\to X_i$, compatible on $B$ by step 3. Projectivity and proper-to-separated give properness of $p_i$. Generic conductor reconstruction gives $(p_1)_K$ an isomorphism and $(p_2)_K=u(p_1)_K$. Lifted markings survive off $B$, with both identities.

source.place: Agent assembly of trait branch pinching (0E25), including universal property and geometric-fibre base change; apply to C_i as well as W.

proof.text: For each $i$, apply finite-complement conductor descent with $r_i:T_i\to C_i$ the regularization and $q_i:W\to T_i$. Here $q_i$ is proper (proper source over separated target), $W$ is regular hence reduced, and $q_i$ is componentwise birational and generically an isomorphism. The branch compatibility was fixed in step 3, and steps 1 and 4 give the pushout hypotheses on $X_i$ and $Y$. It supplies finite closed special sets $Z_i$ and the required isomorphisms off them, including along persistent nodes.

source.place: Agent application of the extracted finite-complement conductor-descent statement, refining 0BFP(1),(2) and open restriction of 0E25 pushouts.

proof.text: For $W\to C_1$, regularization and the selected point blowups give a finite proper chain with nonempty geometrically connected fibres. Apply proper-chain pinching connectedness to this chain and the common $B\to N$; steps 1 and 4 give its hypotheses on $X_1$ and $Y$. Since each $(X_1)_{\bar s}$ is nonempty connected, each $Y_{\bar s}$ is too. Empty $B$ and $n=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Agent application of the extracted proper-chain pinching connectedness statement to the regularization and good-centre blowup chain; geometric-fibre pushout property supplied in step 4.

proof_origin.place: Common regular resolution and point-blowdown universal property, with explicit persistent-node and pinching reductions
